stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, underscoring the growing DoD interest in co-orbital security and space domain awareness (SDA). The company is now valued at $1.6 billion, reflecting the heavy pull from defense contracts. Investors are clearly betting on the need for enhanced security in increasingly crowded orbits.
stories.soWhat: With this kind of cash flow, True Anomaly is positioned to become a key player, but the real question is whether they can deliver on their promises in a timely manner.

stories.head: Anduril teams with L3Harris on SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have joined forces to pursue a tactical SDA constellation contract, which could reshape how the military approaches space-based situational awareness. This collaboration comes at a time when the FY27 budget has earmarked an additional $1.4 billion for space resilience, indicating a serious commitment to strengthening U.S. capabilities.
stories.soWhat: If this bid succeeds, it might not just be a win for these companies, but a signal that the military is serious about integrating commercial tech into its operations.

stories.head: Relativity Space ramps up Terran R production
stories.body: Relativity Space announced plans to expand its Terran R production in Florida, aiming to meet increasing demand for medium-lift launch services. The company’s focus on 3D printing technology is expected to streamline operations and reduce costs, although the timeline for first launches remains vague. Investors are keenly watching if this increased production will translate into actual missions.
stories.soWhat: Relativity's push for production efficiency might just be the edge they need, but they’ll have to prove they can deliver rockets on time, or risk losing ground to more established players.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With $190M in the bank, True Anomaly's strategic decisions will be closely scrutinized as they scale operations.

watchlist.title: Anduril-L3Harris bid results expected soon
watchlist.body: The outcome of their tactical SDA bid could set a precedent for future military partnerships in space.

watchlist.title: Relativity's production timeline may shift
watchlist.body: Any delays in Terran R production could impact their competitive positioning in the launch market.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension could signal more lucrative government contracts on the horizon for data-centric firms.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
